audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was given to Kennen although whys[0] ends 'so it reads even'; Levels 2 and 3 were Skill and Riven although whys[1] and whys[2] say you land the poke trade and own the wave and her HP bar; first item was Riven although whys[5] calls it your spike and says to force every all-in on it.
audit.why: 55.98% over 259 games: Kennen owns levels 2-3, 6 and first item, concedes 4-5 when her combo comes online, and loses the two-item stage to a bruiser-item Riven. The packet chart agrees except at 4-5, where I kept the page's own reading that the stage is hers.
audit.corrected: L1 Skill, L2 Kennen, L3 Kennen, Levels 4-5 Riven, L6 Kennen, first item Kennen, 2+ items Riven.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] describes the late-game flip purely as 'bruiser items' without the cooldown fact that actually causes it.
audit.why: Blade of the Exile is 120/90/60s while Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s at every rank. By her rank 3 she has two ult windows for each of yours, which is why the two-item stage is hers no matter how the poke went.
audit.corrected: Stated the 60s versus 120s gap in spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] says she can 'tank the front of your R channel'. Slicing Maelstrom is not a channel and has no front — Riot's text calls it a summoned storm that strikes nearby enemy champions. The page also tracks Ki Burst without ever giving its cooldown, and never gives Broken Wings' either.
audit.why: Riven kit: Q Broken Wings, flat 13s, 275 range, three casts with the third knocking back; W Ki Burst, 260 range, 11/10/9/8/7s stun; E Valor, 250 range, 10/9/8/7/6s dash plus damage block; R Blade of the Exile, 120/90/60s.
audit.corrected: Valor is a 10s dash-and-shield she uses to eat poke and leave the storm; the numbers to trade around are Broken Wings at 13s and Ki Burst at 11s.

audit.why: packet flagged 'Hold Lightning Rush' in wants.you[1] as a probable wrong name. Lightning Rush is the correct Riot name for Kennen's E and the distance is only the leading word. False positive, no edit.

edits.before: Q-poke from range wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Riven contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: One Q chips her, but with a single ability each and no stun yet neither of you commits — farm and watch which side she walks up on.

edits.before: She hits her level-3 combo here, so if your E is down her Q-W-Q burst trades back hard — chip and respect rather than committing.
edits.after: Her level-3 combo lands here: Broken Wings (13s) into Ki Burst stuns and trades back hard if your E is down, so chip and respect.

edits.before: Once she has bruiser items and your R is down, her three-dash Q stun and reset combo bursts your squishy body in one window.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile falls to 60s at rank 3 against your flat 120 — with bruiser items she gets two ult windows for every one of yours.

edits.before: Use her E shield and second dash to eat your Q poke and tank the front of your R channel
edits.after: Use Valor (E, 10s) to block your Q poke and dash clear of the storm before it stacks marks

notes: Levels 4-5 kept as Riven rather than the packet's 'Skill': whys[3] states plainly that her level-3 combo trades back hard there, and the two directions of the chart should not disagree with the prose that explains them. The claim that Slicing Maelstrom's marks chain 'through her E shield' appears in whys[4], spikes[1] and mid; Riot's text says only that Valor blocks incoming damage, which does not speak to CC application, so I left the claim untouched rather than strengthening or removing it.
